name: vision_multitask_bad
title: The same multi-task trainer with seven planted defects
origin: domain-vision round 2: the dirty twin of vision_multitask. Every finding it produces lands below mlview.minConfidence 0.6, so a VS Code user sees an empty Problems panel on a program with a double sigmoid in it (VIS2-11)

expected.defect: SegmentationHead now ends in torch.sigmoid while MultiTaskLoss still pairs it with nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss
expected.why: the sigmoid is applied twice, so the gradient saturates at both ends and the mask head converges to the class prior
expected.gap: the loss input is a dict subscript (outputs["masks"]) and the criterion is an attribute of a workspace nn.Module (self.mask_bce), so neither operand of the pairing resolves. Same family as VIS2-06.

expected.why: every BatchNorm2d in the shared encoder updates its running statistics from the validation split, and the statistics the next epoch trains with were learned on the data the model is scored against
expected.note: found at confidence 0.59 / possible - below mlview.minConfidence 0.6 - because ConvNormAct is an nn.Sequential SUBCLASS, so MLV301's architecture probe cannot see the BatchNorm2d it holds. See VIS2-11.

expected.defect: the training loader does not shuffle
expected.why: boxes.json lists the records scene by scene, so consecutive batches share a background and the shared encoder's batch statistics track the scene
expected.note: found at 0.54 / possible, below the Problems-panel threshold

expected.why: the graph for a 512x512 segmentation head over the whole validation split is built and dropped
expected.note: found at 0.54 / possible, below the Problems-panel threshold

expected.defect: the running total keeps the live loss tensor
expected.why: a multi-task graph over a 512x512 mask and 64 boxes is retained for the whole epoch
expected.gap: the accumulated value is a dict subscript of a dict returned by a workspace nn.Module, so it carries no LOSS tag - and no untagged_dataflow diagnostic is emitted either.

expected.defect: the validation split is read through the training augmentation pipeline
expected.why: the reported IoU and class accuracy are measured on flipped, rotated and colour-jittered images, so they move between runs for reasons that have nothing to do with the model
expected.gap: MLV114 needs the dataset construction to resolve to a knowledge-table DATASET row; MultiTaskDataset is a workspace Dataset subclass. See VIS2-01.

expected.defect: float16 autocast with no GradScaler anywhere in the workspace
expected.why: fp16 gradients below about 6e-8 flush to zero, which is most of a segmentation gradient, so the mask head trains on nothing and no exception is raised
expected.gap: every MLV208 sub-variant is conditioned on a GradScaler being present, so the one case where the scaler is missing entirely - the commonest AMP mistake there is - cannot fire. The bf16 twin needs no scaler, so the rule would have to read the autocast dtype.

expected.defect: zero_grad() now runs on every batch instead of on the accumulation boundary
expected.why: the gradients of the first accum-1 batches are wiped before the step ever sees them, so the effective batch size is 1/4 of what the configuration says and the learning rate is tuned for a batch that never happens
expected.gap: MLV201 and MLV202 both see a zero_grad and a step in the loop and are satisfied. No rule checks that the zero_grad and the step are on the same side of an accumulation guard, which is the only thing that distinguishes correct accumulation from this.

forbidden.why: there is no sklearn transformer in this project
the validation loader is still built with shuffle=False
the loaders are built inside build_loaders(), reached only from main() under the __main__ guard
optimizer.step() is still called on the accumulation boundary
there is no no_grad region left in this file
OneCycleLR is still stepped inside the batch loop
clip_grad_norm_ still runs between the backward and the step
the mask is still thresholded and the class still argmax-ed before either is compared
the class branch still returns raw logits against nn.CrossEntropyLoss
the model and the criterion are moved with .to(device) and move() moves every batch tensor
the split is two directories on disk
the encoder stages are still wrapped in nn.ModuleList

gaps.what: no rule distinguishes correct gradient accumulation from an accumulation whose zero_grad is outside the guard - the single most common accumulation bug
gaps.evidence: train.py:83 against the clean twin's line 76

gaps.what: MLV208 cannot fire when the GradScaler is absent altogether, which is the commonest fp16 mistake; the rule would have to read the autocast dtype to tell fp16 (needs a scaler) from bf16 (must not have one)
gaps.evidence: train.py:73 dtype=torch.float16 with no GradScaler in the workspace

unsupported.why: LABEL CORRECTED in hardening round 2: MLV211 is not a built rule - it carries the status **later** in docs/ISSUE_RULES.md section 1 - so a label for it can never be satisfied and can never be violated. `analyzer/tests/accuracy/test_accuracy.py::test_every_labelled_code_is_a_real_rule` rejects one, and this row turned that shipped test red. The observation is kept verbatim here so the row can be restored the day the rule ships. Original verdict `forbidden`, original note: the model is still rebound to torch.compile() before the optimizer is built
